event: CELH Piper Sandler 4th Annual Growth Frontiers Conference
rows: CELH Piper Sandler 4th Annual Growth Frontiers Conference
Alani Nu distribution moving to PepsiCo
Long-term gross margin aspiration (apples-to-apples vs Monster)

August expanded PepsiCo deal (~$585M) broken into four elements: (1A) energy captaincy, (1B) Alani Nu into PepsiCo distribution, (3) deeper alignment incl second Board seat + Eric Hanson as President & COO, (4) Rockstar acquisition.
Captaincy gives Celsius control over how much Celsius/Alani Nu/Rockstar shelf space and which SKUs go into PepsiCo-controlled planograms nationally - 'put the fast cars on the track'.
Portfolio at 20%+ energy share - closer to Monster (~28% dollar share) than the next-largest brand (~3%); only Red Bull and Monster previously reached such scale.
Alani Nu transition to PepsiCo on 12/1 moves ~80% of distribution off the fragmented ABI network; convenience and foodservice cited as biggest white space.
Most distribution/assortment gains flow through with the standard reset cadence (Jan-Apr/May), so meaningful realization is Q1/Q2 2026; some independent-convenience pickup in December.
PepsiCo IOD/NOD (inventory-on-display) capability to build large Alani Nu displays in grocery and big box, rolling out Q1/Q2 2026.

Rockstar framed as a turnaround requiring a conservative 'undersell and overdeliver' approach - step one is to stabilize the brand and stop share losses via SKU rationalization; ~$250M is a post-rationalization run rate.
Management declined to commit to Rockstar returning to growth - 'I don't want to make any promises today'; stabilization first (Rockstar once a 10+ share brand).
SKU rationalization underway for core Celsius - ensuring higher-velocity SKUs get greater ACV (orange flavor ~80% should be 95%+).
Promotional toggling across the portfolio so one brand is always on promotion and brands aren't promoted against each other.
Back-half gross margin guided to low 50s (~51%); Q4 under more pressure from FIFO rolling through tariff-affected aluminum cans plus Rockstar transaction noise in Q3/Q4.

Long-term margin aspiration unchanged - mid-50s gross margin on an apples-to-apples basis vs Monster (Monster's reported margin excludes outbound freight which Celsius includes); ~30% EBITDA, no timeline.
Management explicitly declined to discuss 2026 margin - 'we'll see what unfolds over the next quarter or so'.
Celsius first-ever LTO confirmed for Q4 2025; robust 2026 innovation pipeline under evaluation; Alani Nu protein shakes flagged as an exciting adjacent opportunity amid protein's 'moment'.
Energy category exceptional with most brands (Monster, Rebel included) growing double digits; 2024 slump characterized as an industry-wide anomaly now rebounded, helped by easy comps.
Coffee-to-energy substitution: $6-7 coffee vs $3 Celsius; Starbucks conditioning consumers toward cold beverages viewed favorably.
International a conservative, methodical 3-to-5-year play; Australia and Canada jumped to strong share; partner Suntory; ~5% of revenue vs Monster's ~40%.

Management framed Celsius itself as a turnaround story over the past year - stabilized and back to growth, goal to exceed category growth; Alani Nu 'crushing it' with triple-digit growth; now a portfolio-driven company.
Event was entirely a moderated fireside-chat Q&A; no separate prepared remarks.
Explain how the recently expanded PepsiCo deal impacts the portfolio and where management is most excited.

~$585M deal in four elements: (1A) captaincy making Celsius the energy lead within PepsiCo Energy with planogram control; (1B) Alani Nu into PepsiCo distribution from the fragmented ABI network with convenience and foodservice as biggest opportunities (~65% convenience ACV); (3) deeper PepsiCo alignment - second Board seat plus Eric Hanson as President & COO; (4) Rockstar acquisition, step one to stop share losses and stabilize.
Is C-store the focus for distribution upside, and how does each of the three brands change and what comes next?

Alani Nu further along than Celsius was at the PepsiCo transition in MULO, so convenience is its biggest remaining opportunity - tracked plus 100,000+ independent convenience stores via PepsiCo's Medals Program; foodservice (~11-12% of Celsius revenue) is untapped for Alani Nu, well-suited to its college-age female demo.
Looking at each brand separately, what might change - now vs what's ahead for each one?

Captaincy lets the company control how many SKUs of each brand go into PepsiCo planograms, varying by market (Celsius coasts, Alani Nu Central, Rockstar Pacific NW); can sell a 20%+ share portfolio into retailers like Walmart and 7-Eleven; Rockstar adds full-sugar coverage enabling promotional toggling.
How much tougher has it been to get the right assortment vs Red Bull/Monster's concentrated core SKUs, and how much improvement is now possible?

Legacy brands built the category on power SKUs but every brand entering the last 10 years needs a flavor assortment; clear SKU-rationalization opportunity to get higher-velocity SKUs greater ACV (orange flavor ~80% should be 95%+, good performers ~55% to 80%+); exercise underway for core Celsius; excited about the 2026 commercialization approach.
Are there shelf resets to wait for, and how much of the execution is within the company's own control?

Some independent-convenience opportunity in December as Alani Nu rolls in 12/1 (~80% of distribution), but most flow-through follows the standard reset cadence Jan-Apr/May, so meaningful realization is Q1/Q2 2026; PepsiCo IOD/NOD enables large displays in grocery and big box for Alani Nu rolling out Q1/Q2.
Could Rockstar get back to growth, would it have an innovation focus, and what's in store?

Conservative approach - 'undersell and overdeliver'; stabilization the key; many SKUs need consolidating toward top performers and brand DNA (once a 10+ share brand); the ~$250M figure is a post-rationalization run rate per CFO Langhans; declined to make promises - stabilization first.
Where does innovation fit ahead, referencing the Essentials launch ~1.5 years ago?

Innovation important under President Eric Hanson's commercialization approach across three brands; confirmed a Celsius LTO coming in Q4 2025 - the brand's first LTO foray; robust 2026 innovation pipeline under evaluation; Alani Nu protein shakes flagged as an exciting opportunity amid protein's moment.
What is driving the category rebound after the 2024 slump, and how to think about the normalized trajectory?

Category exceptional, most brands (Monster, Rebel) growing double digits; helped by easier comps vs 2024, effective Monster/Red Bull LTO strategies and Alani Nu driving category growth; consumers moving out of coffee given the price gap ($6-7 vs $3); 2024 an industry-wide anomaly now rebounded.
Margin framework - near-term watch-outs given second-half tariff pressure, long-term headroom vs Monster, and any changes to incentive/distribution costs under the new PepsiCo agreement.

Q2 margins strong; aluminum/tariff pressure (absent in Q2 due to FIFO) weighs on H2 - low 50s/~51% as a starting point, Q4 more pressure as FIFO rolls through tariff-affected cans plus Q3/Q4 Rockstar transaction noise; declined to discuss 2026 margin; PepsiCo incentives give it a little enhanced margin; long-term aspiration unchanged - mid-50s gross margin apples-to-apples vs Monster and ~30% EBITDA, no timeline.
Update on the newer international markets and whether the patient, fitness-channel-led approach is the right way to think about it.

Satisfied with progress - Australia and Canada jumped to strong share helped by distribution capability and right retail/distributor partners (7-Eleven, Suntory); conservative, methodical build judged on the bottom line, fitness channel drives brand equity; international a 3-to-5-year play, ~5% of revenue (lower post-Alani Nu) vs Monster's ~40%.
Closing thoughts / what investors might be missing
Closing thoughts on what investors might be missing or anything else to consider.

Framed Celsius as a turnaround story over the past year - after high peaks ~2020 to mid-2024 and 2024 difficulties, the brand stabilized and returned to growth with the goal of exceeding category growth; feels good heading into 2026; Alani Nu crushing it with triple-digit growth; restructured into a portfolio-driven company.
